function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of places you can order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or just want it delivered right to your door.

| Option | What it offers | How to get it |
|--------|----------------|---------------|
| **Local bakeries** | Freshly baked cakes, often customizable (flavors, sizes, designs). Many have a strong reputation in their community. | Search “bakeries near me” on Google Maps or Yelp; call or visit their website to place an order. |
| **Specialty cake shops** | Artisan cakes, wedding cakes, themed cakes (e.g., birthday, corporate). Usually offer design consultations. | Look up “cake shops” + your city; many have Instagram pages showcasing past work. |
| **Online marketplaces** | Sites like Etsy let you browse independent bakers who ship nationwide. Great for unique flavors or dietary restrictions. | Browse “cakes” on Etsy, filter by shipping location, read seller ratings. |
| **Grocery store delivery** | Whole Foods, Kroger, Safeway, etc. often carry pre‑made cakes and sometimes custom orders. | Use the store’s app or website; select “delivery” and choose a cake from the bakery section. |
| **Food‑delivery apps** | Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, SkipTheDishes (Canada), Deliveroo (UK). Many partner with local bakeries and restaurants. | Open the app, search “cakes” or “bakery,” pick a vendor, customize, and checkout. |
| **Same‑day delivery services** | Instacart, Shipt, Amazon Fresh. Some partners deliver freshly baked goods from local stores. | Sign up, add a cake to your cart, schedule a delivery window. |
| **National chains** | Costco, Walmart, Target, Trader Joe’s. They sell pre‑made cakes in various sizes. | Order online through their websites or apps; choose pickup or delivery. |
| **Custom cake designers** | Companies like Cake Boss, Sweet Treats, or local “custom cake” businesses. Offer design services, photo uploads, and sometimes 3‑D printing. | Contact via phone or website; discuss theme, size, flavor, and budget. |

### Tips for ordering

1. **Check reviews & photos** – especially for custom or online orders.  
2. **Ask about dietary options** – gluten‑free, vegan, sugar‑free, etc.  
3. **Order early** – most bakeries recommend ordering at least 24–48 hrs in advance for custom cakes.  
4. **Confirm delivery details** – address, contact number, preferred time slot.  
5. **Tip the baker** – if you’re ordering directly from a small shop, consider adding a tip or sending a thank‑you note.

If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up specific bakeries or delivery partners that serve your area!
